robonexus.title: ROBONEXUS
robonexus.status: Through to the next stage. The competition is now in March 2027.
robonexus.summary: A capture-the-flag robot that plays the first 45 seconds of every match on its own.
robonexus.body: The first prototype is built and driving. Every motor and both grippers are programmed, and the robot tracks its own position with OpenVINS visual-inertial odometry from a stereo camera and IMU, calibrated with Kalibr. I designed the robot and its URDF, built the Gazebo simulation it was developed in, and raised ₩6,000,000 to fund it.
robonexus.next: Moving the mission-control code and motion planner from the simulation onto the robot, starting the second robot, and ordering sheet metal for the competition build.

fair.title: FAIR Lab
fair.summary: Keeping a robot connected as it drives deep into a building, using other robots as radio relays.
fair.body: I set up a Rajant Cardinal mesh network, with Ackermann cars as the relays and the lab’s chain robot as the client. I programmed an obstacle-aware model of signal strength (RSSI), calibrated it against our own radios, and tested it on a hospital floor I imported into Gazebo. Getting the chain robot and the relays into one simulation meant bridging mismatched ROS and Gazebo versions; the relays now reach their waypoints to within 2–8 cm.
fair.next: Making the relays move on their own, following the signal strength to keep the client connected.
specs: Robots|Chain robot client, two Ackermann relays
Stack|ROS 2, Gazebo, Docker on two NUCs

angel.title: Angel Robotics
angel.summary: A two-armed robot on a cart that gets around by pushing the floor with its arms.
angel.body: One month, a team of three, and hardware that had barely left the lab: Angel Robotics’ new PHACT actuators, which cancel their own friction in real time so the joint delivers clean, measurable torque, driven from an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin with 64 GB of memory. I worked on the design, assembly and programming: I built the arm’s URDF from CAD, taught its motions by imitation learning, and paired the robot with SLAM, using Orbbec depth cameras and NVIDIA’s cuVSLAM, to explore and map the space around it. Angel Robotics recognized me for giving the most feedback on their hardware.

ee405.title: EE405
ee405.summary: A rover with an arm that finds blocks, picks them up, and drives itself through a course.
ee405.body: A mecanum-wheeled rover with a six-axis arm. The arm locates blocks by their ArUco markers and grasps them using forward and inverse kinematics. The rover maps the course with SLAM, then drives it with Nav2, which I retuned for its mecanum wheels: omnidirectional MPPI control, A* planning, and a speed cap hidden in the velocity smoother lifted from 0.26 to 0.6 m/s.
specs: Course|AI & Vision for Robotics, Electronics Design Lab
Navigation|SLAM, Nav2 with MPPI and A*

robonexus.title: ROBONEXUS
robonexus.text: A mecanum-wheeled robot for a CTF competition: secure flags on your side or steal your opponent's flags. The initial 45 seconds are autonomous. I designed the robot, built the simulation, and trained the flag detector on 5,000+ synthetic renders on Unity.

drone.title: Autonomous Drone
drone.text: A quadrotor equipped with 2x Intel RealSense + Nvidia Orin Nano to achieve local on-board autonomous flight. The mission had the drone read a riddle, hand it to a language model, pick the gate the answer points to, avoid what is in the way, then find the correct target location and land on it.

car.title: Self-driving racing car
car.text: A Raspberry Pi car I built end to end. It follows a white line to the grid under a convolutional network, waits for the lights, then hands over to a PID loop on ultrasonic range to race a walled circuit. Two control paradigms, one vehicle, swapping mid-run.

caricature.title: Caricature drawing robot
caricature.text: A dead 3D printer stripped for its steppers and rebuilt as a plotter that draws your face back at you. The interesting part is between the photo and the pen: the portrait becomes a graph, and Dijkstra orders the strokes so the pen spends its time drawing instead of travelling.

personal.heading: Off the clock
paragraphs: I game, and I run the servers I game on — which is where the networking and Linux on my skills list actually came from. Nothing teaches you DNS and port forwarding like a friend saying they can’t connect.

I cook, a lot. I like bikes. And I am genuinely interested in the business side of engineering, not just the build — writing the ROBONEXUS proposal and walking away with ₩6,000,000 was one of the more satisfying things I have done, and it was not a technical problem.
